tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay extending the prior unknown-outcome/idempotency result. The fixture assumes one provider idempotency token T4 is stably bound to prepared transition S3 and payload digest D4, but the provider token/result retention window expires before a later scheduled retry. Trace A retries after expiry without any durable repository post-effect receipt. Trace B has a durable repository effect-committed tombstone/result receipt written after provider success but before successor finalization, then reconstructs finalization from that receipt after provider retention expires. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

trace_A_expired_token_no_durable_post_ef.observation: After provider retention expires, repository state cannot distinguish 'effect never happened' from 'effect happened but acknowledgement was lost'. Reusing T4 is no longer guaranteed idempotent if the provider has forgotten it, while minting a new token is plainly a new logical request. Automatic retry can therefore duplicate the effect; refusing retry preserves duplicate safety but may permanently lose the useful result.

trace_B_durable_effect_committed_tombsto.observation: For this exact trace, provider retention expiry no longer creates duplicate issuance because durable repository evidence already proves that the logical effect reached a terminal accepted state and identifies the result needed for finalization. The provider is not consulted after expiry.

derived_minimum_durable_fields: Exact prepared transition identity and predecessor/successor generation tuple.
Authority/fencing epoch binding the effect to the permitted claimant.
Stable provider token/effect identity and exact payload digest; a token alone without payload binding is insufficient.
Provider accepted-operation/effect identity or equivalent terminal identity.
Unambiguous terminal outcome marker proving whether the logical effect occurred.
Result digest plus repository-resident result material or a durable non-expiring result handle sufficient to reconstruct the useful outcome without provider replay.
Commit stage indicating effect_committed but successor_not_yet_finalized so later invocations do not reissue the effect.
CAS/readback linkage from predecessor through prepared transition to the post-effect receipt before successor visibility.

impossibility_window.condition: The effect may have occurred, no repository post-effect receipt/result identity became durable, and the provider idempotency/result retention guarantee has already expired.
impossibility_window.result: No repository-only retry rule can simultaneously guarantee both no duplicate logical effect and recovery of the useful result from the information remaining in this fixture. A safe design must either make a post-effect receipt durable before the provider evidence can disappear, or require a provider retention guarantee that exceeds the maximum supported checkpoint-resume horizon.

weak_expiry_retry_rule.rule: If S3 is still prepared after the provider idempotency window expires and no repository result is present, retry the effect once using either the old token or a newly derived token.
weak_expiry_retry_rule.falsification: In Trace A the original effect already occurred. After expiry the old token may be treated as unseen and a new token is necessarily a fresh request, so either form of retry can create a second logical effect. The rule is therefore not duplicate-safe.

observations: Idempotency retention is part of the safety boundary, not a convenience parameter: once provider memory expires, a stable token ceases to prove duplicate suppression unless the provider contract explicitly says otherwise.
A durable post-effect receipt changes the recovery problem from 'should the effect be retried?' to 'can finalization be replayed?', which can be solved repository-locally for the exact modeled trace.

A tombstone that merely says 'attempted' is insufficient. To prevent duplicate issuance and still recover the useful outcome, it must durably distinguish terminal effect occurrence and bind the exact result/effect identity to the prepared transition.

There remains an unavoidable crash window between external effect occurrence and durable post-effect receipt unless provider-side idempotency/result retention covers that interval and the later checkpoint-resume horizon.
inference: For the exact retention-expiry fixture tested, safe recurring-Chat recovery requires a two-layer contract: provider-side idempotency/result reconstruction must cover the interval until a repository post-effect receipt becomes durable, and the repository must then preserve enough terminal effect/result evidence to avoid any provider retry after provider retention can expire. If both provider evidence and durable post-effect repository evidence are absent, the unknown-outcome ambiguity is information-theoretically unresolved within this fixture. This does not prove any concrete Chat-exposed provider supplies the required semantics or that the full Phase-1 root is satisfied.
